standard_prerequisites.name: Riemann bilinear identity
standard_prerequisites.statement: Standard named fact: for meromorphic differentials on a compact Riemann surface, the period pairing equals the sum of residues of the product against a primitive inside a fundamental polygon.
standard_prerequisites.use: Load-bearing: the proof rewrites the pairing of (oint v_0, oint Qtilde/v_0) as a residue sum (109) and reduces the hbar^k coefficients to residues (121) and (122).

standard_prerequisites.name: Variational formulas (51), (52)
standard_prerequisites.statement: Delivered in context (author Proposition environment, source lines 398-404): derivatives of the period matrix and of normalized holomorphic differentials against period coordinates are contour integrals.
standard_prerequisites.use: Load-bearing: the proof evaluates the pairing of Qtilde/v_0 against delta oint v_0 via (111) and (114).

standard_prerequisites.name: Period-pairing variational identity (Lemma 3.6)
standard_prerequisites.statement: Delivered in the unit as its own card (Lem_1): the identity (78)/(79) rewriting the pairing with delta oint w_2 as a boundary integral plus a (w_1 w_2/v)-pairing term.
standard_prerequisites.use: Load-bearing: the proof cites Lemma 3.6 (source line 740) to rewrite the pairings in (106) as (116) and (117).

standard_prerequisites.name: Connectedness of the stratum
standard_prerequisites.statement: Theorem 1.3 of Chen-Gendron (cited as chen2021classification): generically (outside the hyperelliptic locus for g >= 3) the stratum Q_{g,n}, hence Q_{g,n}[r], is connected.
standard_prerequisites.use: Load-bearing: the arbitrary-pair case joins Q_0 and Q_1 by a path and applies the nearby-pair identity telescopically (source lines 816-829).

standard_prerequisites.name: Stokes' theorem and the Poincare lemma
standard_prerequisites.statement: Standard named facts of multivariable calculus on manifolds.
standard_prerequisites.use: Load-bearing: (79) follows from (78) by Stokes (source lines 654-657 of the Lemma 3.6 proof) and the closed-form hypothesis is integrated locally by the Poincare lemma (source lines 831-832).

core_obligations: Nearby case: differentiate the period coordinates in hbar (101), expand the potential theta_1 by the pairing (77) into the series (105)/(106), evaluate the hbar^1 coefficient through the residue identity (109) and the variational formulas (111)/(114) to get (115), and the hbar^k coefficients through Lemma 3.6 (116)/(117) plus the residue-vanishing degeneration argument (124)-(125) to get (123).
Resummation: recognize the series as the regularized period difference (128) and assemble (129) for nearby differentials.

Arbitrary case: connect Q_0 to Q_1 by a path using connected-ness (Chen-Gendron Theorem 1.3), telescope (129) along a finite subcover to (131), and read off both statements of the proposition (differentiate (131) for part 1; Poincare lemma for part 2).
proof_roadmap: Three-stage argument: hbar-expansion of periods and the potential near Q_0 with residue calculus for each coefficient, resummation into the regularized period difference, then a path-telescoping argument over the connected stratum to reach arbitrary pairs.
difficulty_reason: H3整链：510-832在branched double covers上固定Abelian integral坐标求period variations时处理跨homology cycle的jump，建立修正Riemann bilinear identity；对sqrt(Q0+hQtilde)展开symplectic potential，按branch-point/pole residues拆分并用holomorphic lifted expression证明高阶branch residues消失，处理端点regularization，再沿connected moduli路径有限覆盖把局部identity拼成全局potential difference与generating function。难点是移动分支/period jumps、regularized pole integrals及全局symplectic对应，不以长式展开判H3。
